Foam sweep fit with the two-face column contact law

Built 2026-10-29 20:58 from files on disk by projects/digital_instron_v2/sweep_report.py.

SummaryDataShoe and lastContact lawResultsOpen issuesReproduce

1. Summary

One material is fitted per shoe to its Instron foam sweep: a two-term Hyperfoam (Ogden-Hill) equilibrium network with one Maxwell branch and a Jenkin (spring-slider) branch, plus the shear-layer fraction, 9 parameters. Every sweep trace is replayed through the GPU column bed with the new two-face column contact law (ColumnBed): each midsole column has a top pressed by the last and a bottom that lands on the platen. The fit uses train cycles only; validate and repeat traces are scored, not fitted.

2. Data

Each shoe was cycled on the Instron with a full-foot last at a 0.5 s period. The programmed grid is 4 stance times (160, 200, 240, 280 ms) x 6 peak forces (800 to 2800 N in 400 N steps), 100 cycles per condition. Each condition gives two phase-averaged traces (501 samples per cycle):

  • train: mean of cycles 90-98, used by the fit;
  • validate: mean of cycles 99-100, only scored.

The programmed 320 ms block is in fact a second copy of the 200 ms block (same loaded duration). It is not a new stance time; it is used as a repeatability check (the "repeat" traces).

3. Shoe and last

The last pose over the midsole column grid comes from registration.register_last, run inside the fit. Inputs are the shoe_prep left/column_grid.npz files (canonical frame, heel at -x). The preload contact uses a linear column modulus of 3 x the initial equilibrium shear modulus; it only sets the 20 N preload estimate, and the rest pitch changes by less than 0.3 deg when it is halved or doubled.

Method

  • Last up = normal of the square attachment plate. It agrees with the stud axis to 0.002 deg. It is 3.3 deg off the STL +y axis, so last pitch and roll are fixed by the attachment and never fitted.
  • Last heel = the narrow end (23 mm narrower). The ball tread (lowest plantar point) sits at 70% of the length. The heel seat is 5.1 mm above the ball tread.
  • Shoe heel = the thicker and narrower end (canonical_frame).
  • The midsole rocks on the platen. Its pitch and roll minimize the potential energy of the 20 N preload on linear columns. A rocker sole tips until the last contact is balanced over its platen contact.
  • Last x, y and yaw minimize the soft-L1 spread of the last-to-top clearance. The last tread (surface within 45 deg of horizontal) must stay inside the midsole outline. z is set at first contact.

Caveats

  • FR3: the last tread just fits the narrow FR3 waist. The outline sets x, y and yaw, not the surface fit.
  • First contact is at the heel cup rim and heel. The forefoot footbed sits 5-9 mm below the last plantar surface.
  • The last side (left) comes from its file name; the shoe side evidence is not definitive.
  • The midsole is rigid while it rocks. The preload uses linear columns.

4. Contact law: two-face columns

The midsole is a grid of vertical columns (about 6 mm spacing). Each column has rest thickness L, footprint area A, and two unknowns: the downward displacement of its top, t, and of its bottom, b. The compression is c = t - b. The last presses the tops; the platen supports the bottoms. Both contacts are one-way.

compression            c = t - b,     0 <= c < L
last on the top        t >= d - g     (d = last stroke, g = rest gap; the last pushes, never pulls)
platen on the bottom   b <= h         (h = rest clearance of the bottom over the platen)
outside the last       top free

energy   E = sum_i A_i W(c_i)  +  1/2 sum_faces k_ij [ (t_i - t_j)^2 + (b_i - b_j)^2 ]
         W'(c) = p(c/L): two-term Hyperfoam equilibrium pressure + Maxwell overstress + slider stress
         k_ij  = s mu_eq (L_i + L_j) / 2,    mu_eq = (G1 + G2) f_eq   (Pasternak shear layer, s fitted)

reactions   T_i = last on top i (held tops only),   R_i = platen on bottom i (landed bottoms only)
balance     sum_i T_i = sum_i R_i   (the shear terms cancel over the bed)

No cross term. The energy has one shear layer at the tops and one at the bottoms, and nothing that couples a top difference to a bottom difference. An earlier variant had such a cross term. It lifted thick edge columns off the platen, so it was dropped.

Four column states (for columns under the last tread):

  • held, landed: the last presses the top and the bottom stands on the platen; the foam carries the load straight through.
  • held, floating: the last presses the top, the bottom is in the air; the column passes its load sideways to neighbours through the bottom shear layer.
  • open, landed: the bottom stands on the platen, the last does not touch the top; it carries only the shear its neighbours put on it.
  • open, floating: neither face touches; the column only follows its neighbours.

Columns outside the last tread have a free top and are only landed or floating.

Range of shear support. A held column with a floating bottom is supported only by shear from landed neighbours. In the continuum limit the bottom-layer stiffness per area is s mu_eq L and the foam stiffness per area is E/L with E = 2 mu_eq at small strain, so the support decays over a length lambda = sqrt(s mu_eq L^2 / E) = L sqrt(s/2), a few millimetres for 20-35 mm thick columns at the fitted s, and less once the foam stiffens at large strain. A floating region much wider than that gets almost no support.

Solver. One CUDA block per world runs red-black Gauss-Seidel sweeps. Each column update solves its local 2x2 problem exactly over the active constraints. A step limiter (fraction-to-boundary, factor 0.5) lets one update close at most half of the remaining open thickness L - c, so a far-off step cannot jump into the foam lock-up near c = L. Converged states are not changed by it.

Physical checks. A replayed cycle counts as physical only if T and R are finite, the platen only pushes, and |sum T - sum R| stays within 2% of the peak load every frame (last_replay.physical). A cycle that fails returns NaN. In the fit, a start whose own replay is not physical stops with a message, a Jacobian column is differenced from the other side, and the final scoring raises instead of writing a result. So a broken solve fails loudly instead of giving a smooth wrong force.

5. Results per shoe

Train loss is the mean squared residual of core.force_residual (force over the cycle, loop area x5, peak x6, all relative). Each start is a bounded least-squares solve with up to 80 residual evaluations; all starts run together on the GPU. Cells marked red miss at least one 10% gate (peak, RMSE, loading or unloading RMSE, loop area).

G1, G2 and alpha2 trade off between near-best starts, but the derived mu_eq, f_eq and tau stay tight. The second Hyperfoam term acts as a densification wall whose onset is identified and whose steepness is not; see the second-term section below.

7. Open issues

  • Hysteresis at low force. The loop-area error is largest at 800 N (FR3 0.7-2.0%, Dev3Elite 0.2-2.8%).
  • Load outside the last. Columns beyond the last tread carry FR3 15.2-18.4%, Dev3Elite 6.4-8.1% of platen load at peak through shear. This share is not measured; a pressure-mat test would check it.
  • Shoe and last side. The left last is assumed from its file name; the side has not been independently confirmed.
  • Runner validation. The fitted shoes use the shared column-bed kernel, but gait results still need comparison with measured references.

8. Reproduce

From the repository root, split the raw sweeps, fit each shoe and rebuild this report.

uv run --extra dev -m projects.digital_instron_v2.sweep_split
uv run --extra dev -m projects.digital_instron_v2 fit --shoe DigitalInstron/puma-fast-r-nitro-elite-3 --sweep DigitalInstron/FoamSweep/processed/FR3 --out DigitalInstron/FoamSweep/fit/puma-fast-r-nitro-elite-3
uv run --extra dev -m projects.digital_instron_v2 fit --shoe DigitalInstron/puma-deviate-nitro-elite-3 --sweep DigitalInstron/FoamSweep/processed/Dev3Elite --out DigitalInstron/FoamSweep/fit/puma-deviate-nitro-elite-3
uv run --extra dev -m projects.digital_instron_v2.sweep_report
